Efficient-score screening for GLMs and special families

Source: R/sis_glm.R
sis_glm.Rd

Screen predictors using one null/nuisance fit and native column reductions, without fitting a separate model for every predictor. Dense matrices stay dense and sparse matrices stay sparse.

Usage

sis_glm(
  X,
  y,
  family = gaussian(),
  weights = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  nsis = NULL,
  return_stats = TRUE,
  nuisance = NULL,
  nonnegative = FALSE,
  iterative = FALSE,
  niter = 10L,
  nthreads = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

X

Numeric predictor matrix, dense or sparse, with observations in rows.

y

Response as in L0glm.fit(): a numeric vector or independent-channel matrix for ordinary/NB models; factors, class labels or count matrices for multinomial; or survival::Surv(time, status) for right-censored Cox models.

family

Any standard GLM family/link, a fixed-theta negative-binomial family, or mgcv::nb(), mgcv::multinom(K) or mgcv::cox.ph().

weights

Nonnegative prior weights: a scalar, observation vector, or observation-by-channel matrix for ordinary/NB models. Multinomial and Cox use shared row weights.

offset

Known linear-predictor offsets: a scalar, observation vector, or observation-by-channel/category matrix. Cox uses a vector.

nsis

Number of predictors retained, capped at ncol(X). Defaults to min(p, max(1, floor(n/log(n)))). No size guarantees true-feature retention.

return_stats

Return all statistics and their full ranking, default TRUE. Use FALSE for large designs to retain only the top predictors.

nuisance

Optional numeric nuisance design. NULL uses an intercept, except for Cox, which has none. An explicit zero-column matrix requests no nuisance terms. Include an intercept explicitly when supplying other nuisance predictors. Constant Cox nuisance columns are omitted.

nonnegative

Use one-sided scores for nonnegative candidate effects. Nuisance terms remain unrestricted. Ignored for multinomial CLR effects.

iterative

Use offset-based iterative SIS (ISIS), default FALSE.

niter

Maximum ISIS rounds, default 10. Stops when the candidate set repeats, since refitting that same subproblem would give the same fit.

nthreads

Positive integer OpenMP thread count for predictor screening, NULL (default) uses the physical core count, falling back to one if detection is unavailable. Capped at logical processors and predictor count. Builds without OpenMP use one thread. Does not change BLAS threads or outcome-fitting parallelism; use screen.nthreads in L0glm.fit().

...

Named L0glm.fit() arguments for ISIS, such as lambda, start, intercept, always.include, grouped, normalize and solver controls. ISIS defaults to lambda="gic", start=NULL, relaxed=TRUE and parallelize=FALSE. Coefficient-shaped starts/prior means use the original predictor dimensions, optionally including an added intercept; they are subset internally. Scalar start=1 retains its normalized-coordinate meaning. Initial zero starts remain excluded, except mandatory terms.

Value

A list with decreasing-score indices, top_statistics, nsis, family, link, fitted theta for NB, and nthreads (screening threads actually used). With return_stats=TRUE, ranking lists all predictor indices and stats contains feature, stat, sign, rank and keep. Signs are NA for multichannel/joint scores. Full statistics/ranking are otherwise NULL. ISIS additionally returns a full-dimension L0glm_fit in fit, its sparse coefficients, the best round's candidates, resolved lambda, history (including GIC, deviance and support size), best_iteration, iterations, converged and elapsed seconds. Its indices are retained nonzero or mandatory predictors in original column order; nsis counts these and screen_size records the screening batch size. Optional statistics/ranking describe the screen preceding the chosen fit, with keep updated to its retained rows. top_statistics is NULL for ISIS. The returned fit accepts new data with all original columns in stats::predict().

Details

For an ordinary GLM let \(s_i=v_i(y_i-\mu_i)\dot\mu_i/ (\phi V(\mu_i))\) and \(h_i=v_i\dot\mu_i^2/(\phi V(\mu_i))\), evaluated at the nuisance fit. For candidate \(x\) and nuisance design \(N\), $$U=x^Ts-x^THN(N^THN)^+N^Ts,\qquad I=x^THx-x^THN(N^THN)^+N^THx,$$ with \(H=\operatorname{diag}(h)\). Rank \(U^2/I\), or \(\max(U,0)^2/I\) for a one-sided candidate. Unidentifiable columns get zero; ties use original column order. Noncanonical derivatives retain their sign. Free dispersion uses the null-fit Pearson statistic/residual degrees of freedom. NB theta is fitted or fixed according to the supplied family.

Independent channels contribute separate statistics, preventing cancellation of opposite effects. Multinomial uses the exact joint score/information in orthonormal contrasts of the CLR plane; grouped ranking is invariant to category relabeling. Cox uses exact weighted Breslow risk sets, ties and nuisance adjustment. Quasi families do not require a likelihood.

Native kernels avoid X^2 and scaled design copies. Independent channels use diagonal information; multinomial accumulates curvature from probabilities without an observation-by-category-squared array. Without full statistics, a bounded heap selects top predictors. Screening can miss weak/suppressor effects and does not certify a global L0 optimum. Screening threads process separate predictors with unchanged within-column summation order. Thread-local top-candidate heaps are merged deterministically, including ties in original column order. Errors and interrupts are handled on the main R thread; no design-sized copies are made for threading.

With iterative=TRUE, add the fitted linear predictor to the original offset for screening, merge new candidates with current nonzero/mandatory rows, and refit on the original responses and original offsets. Each round starts afresh; this does not reintroduce coefficients within an individual BAR fit. Preset lambda and GIC use the original selectable predictor count. The lowest-GIC round is returned, using the metrics scoring mean floor of 1e-8. For quasi families without a likelihood/GIC, return the last round. nuisance must be NULL for ISIS: put mandatory covariates in X and pass always.include instead. Intercept defaults match L0glm.fit(). converged describes repetition of the outer candidate set; inner-fit convergence diagnostics remain in fit$convergence. L0glm.fit() also exposes this workflow through screen="SIS" or screen="ISIS", with automatic ISIS for ultra-wide eligible designs. Its small default ISIS batch and other screened-fit defaults are documented in that function; pass nsis explicitly to match a standalone call exactly.

See also

L0glm.fit()

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 150; p <- 300
X <- matrix(rnorm(n*p),n,p)
beta <- c(1,-1,.8,-.8,rep(0,p-4))
y <- as.numeric(X%*%beta)+rnorm(n)
screen <- sis_glm(X,y,nsis=40,return_stats=FALSE)
screen$indices
threaded <- sis_glm(X,y,nsis=40,return_stats=FALSE,nthreads=4)
identical(threaded$indices,screen$indices)

# Independent channels are screened jointly without signed cancellation.
multi <- sis_glm(X,cbind(y,-y),nsis=40,return_stats=FALSE)
multi$indices

# Conditional screening includes the specified nuisance design.
conditional <- sis_glm(X,y,nuisance=cbind(1,X[,1]),nsis=40)
head(conditional$stats[conditional$ranking,])

# Offset-based outer ISIS; each candidate fit starts afresh.
iterated <- sis_glm(X,y,nsis=40,iterative=TRUE,niter=10,return_stats=FALSE)
iterated$history
coef(iterated$fit)                 # sparse, all original predictor rows
head(predict(iterated$fit,X[1:5,,drop=FALSE]))

# The same full-dimension model through the main fitting interface.
fit <- L0glm.fit(X,y,screen="ISIS",nsis=40,screen.maxit=10,screen.nthreads=4)
fit$screening$history
coef(fit)
# screen="auto" (the default) enables ISIS only for ultra-wide eligible designs.
# Use screen="none" to fit the full design directly.

if (requireNamespace("mgcv",quietly=TRUE)) {
  counts <- rnbinom(n,mu=exp(.5+.4*X[,1]),size=2)
  nb <- sis_glm(X,counts,family=mgcv::nb(),nsis=20,return_stats=FALSE)
  nb$theta
  classes <- factor(sample(letters[1:3],n,TRUE))
  multinomial <- sis_glm(X,classes,family=mgcv::multinom(2),
                        nsis=20,return_stats=FALSE)
}
if (requireNamespace("mgcv",quietly=TRUE) && requireNamespace("survival",quietly=TRUE)) {
  time <- rexp(n,exp(.5*X[,1]))
  outcome <- survival::Surv(pmin(time,2),time<=2)
  cox <- sis_glm(Matrix::Matrix(X,sparse=TRUE),outcome,
                family=mgcv::cox.ph(),nsis=20,return_stats=FALSE)
}
